overview: Jelling preserves the ways tenth-century Danish rulers expressed ancestry, authority and religious change through monuments and inscriptions.

items.text: Gorm's smaller runestone commemorated Thyra. Harald's larger stone commemorated both parents.
Harald's inscription claimed rule over Denmark and Norway and the conversion of the Danes. It is a royal claim, not a precise boundary survey or proof of uniform conversion.
Two large turf-built mounds stand beside the stones.
A sequence of wooden churches at the site and Christian imagery on Harald's stone show changes in royal religious representation.

sources.title: UNESCO: Jelling Mounds, Runic Stones and Church
